title: Arrow Functions
summary: Arrow functions are a compact syntax for writing functions. The key difference from regular functions is that they do not have their own 'this' binding — they inherit 'this' from the surrounding scope. This makes them ideal for callbacks. The concise body form (no curly braces) implicitly returns the single expression. Returning an object literal from a concise body requires wrapping the object in parentheses to avoid ambiguity with a function body.
keyPoints: Syntax: const fn = (params) => expression  OR  const fn = (params) => { statements }
Concise body (no {}) implicitly returns the expression — no return keyword needed
Single parameter: parentheses around the parameter are optional
Zero parameters: empty parentheses () are required
Returning an object literal from concise body: wrap in () to avoid syntax confusion
Arrow functions do not have their own 'this' — they inherit from the enclosing scope
Cannot be used as constructors (no new keyword)

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a valid concise-body arrow function that returns title + ' (' + year + ')'?
options: const fmt = title, year => title + ' (' + year + ')'
exercises.explanation: With two or more parameters you need parentheses. The concise body has no {}, so the expression is implicitly returned. The -> syntax does not exist in JavaScript.

exercises.prompt:
What does this function return?

const toSummary = movie => { title: movie.title }
exercises.explanation: JavaScript interprets the {} as a function body, not an object literal. The label 'title:' is a statement label, and movie.title is evaluated but not returned. The function returns undefined. Fix: wrap in parentheses: movie => ({ title: movie.title })
Single parameter needs no parentheses. The concise body implicitly returns the expression, so no return keyword is needed.

options: const toCard = movie => { title: movie.title, rating: movie.rating }
const toCard = movie => ({ title: movie.title, rating: movie.rating })
const toCard = movie => return { title: movie.title, rating: movie.rating }
const toCard = (movie) { return { title: movie.title, rating: movie.rating } }
exercises.answer: const toCard = movie => ({ title: movie.title, rating: movie.rating })
exercises.explanation: Object literals in a concise body must be wrapped in () so JavaScript knows {} is an object, not a function body.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const ratings = [8.8, 7.3, 9.1, 6.5]

Which expression uses an arrow function to return only ratings above 8.0?
exercises.explanation: The concise body arrow function implicitly returns the expression. The version with {} needs an explicit return keyword. The -> syntax does not exist in JavaScript.
